results.evidence: No source gives a season window for the face. A private party climbed it in firm neve on 13-14 July 2019 and park climbing rangers found it climbable on 25 July 2017, which undercuts the row's "July risky" as much as the May-June window, while another party in 2017 was turned back by open bergschrunds. What would settle it: a route description that states the usual climbing window.

The route's own long-standing description gives the harder right-hand variation "a couple of ice steps, AI 2-3" (its headline chip reads AI3-4, but the text describes AI2-3 steps); The Mountaineers route summary also gives AI2-3 ice steps; an independent party on 13 July 2019 graded the face IV, AI2, 60 degrees, finding only a small vein of AI2 at the start of the grade IV variation. No source grades it as water ice (WI), so the WI3-4 chip is replaced with the alpine-ice grade the row's prose already states.

results.correct_value: Leave Ptarmigan Ridge near 8,200-8,300 ft, descend ~1,000 ft to the North Mowich Glacier, then climb the North Mowich roped to camps near 9,600-10,200 ft below the face; the South Mowich is not on the approach.
results.evidence: The Central Mowich Face route description says to follow the climbers' path up the lower part of Ptarmigan Ridge and at 8,300 ft leave the ridge and descend 1,000 ft to the North Mowich Glacier. A 13 July 2019 party dropped off the ridge just over 8,200 ft, reached the edge of the North Mowich at 7,200 ft, roped up, and climbed the glacier to a bivy at 10,200 ft above the bergschrund; park climbing rangers in 2017 camped at 9,600 ft between the North Mowich and Edmunds glaciers, and the North Mowich Headwall description also puts the bivy in a bowl near 10,000 ft reached up the North Mowich. So hazards[3] (drop onto the glacier, ascend it to camp) is right; the approach/variant/pitch text that camps on the ridge at 9,600-10,300 ft and then drops, and the partner/hazard text naming the South Mowich, are rewritten.

patches.find: Continue ascending the ridge's lower apron until it narrows above Observation Rock; established bivy sites (some with old wind-break rock walls) sit around 9,600-10,300 ft near the base of the North Mowich/Edmunds Glaciers, used as camps for Mowich Face, Edmunds Headwall, and Ptarmigan Ridge alike. From camp, drop and traverse across the North Mowich Glacier (roped, watch for recent rockfall debris crossing the ice) to gain the base of the Mowich Face proper.
patches.replace: Continue up the ridge's lower apron to roughly 8,300 ft, above Observation Rock, then leave the ridge and descend about 1,000 ft of loose rock and old snow to the edge of the North Mowich Glacier. Rope up there and climb the North Mowich (watch for recent rockfall debris crossing the ice) to camps at roughly 9,600-10,200 ft near the Edmunds divide, just below the Mowich Face proper.

results.evidence: Searches found no stated one-way distance for the Mowich Face approach. The row's 13 mi itinerary starts at Mowich Lake, while dist_km (18 mi) is consistent with adding part of the walk-in now required to reach Mowich Lake, so the two may measure different starting points. What would settle it: a source stating the one-way distance from the current access point to the face.

results.correct_value: Descent is about 7.5 miles; the 8-10 hour figure is not a descent time
results.evidence: The "7.5 miles / 8-10 hours" pairing matches a guide service itinerary where 8-10 hours is the WHOLE day from Ingraham Flats up to the summit and down to Paradise, not the descent alone. A second guide service gives the full Muir-summit-Muir-Paradise summit day as 10-14 hours with the descent taking roughly half the ascent time, and the park route brief says the descent from Columbia Crest to Camp Muir takes about two-thirds of the ascent time. So the 12-hour summit day in the itinerary/timing is consistent and the 8-10 hour descent claim is the error; the hours are removed from the descent sentence.

patches.replace: Total descent is about 7.5 miles, and it usually takes well under the time spent climbing up.

results.evidence: Sources still split: a guide service gives the summit-to-Paradise descent as 7.5 miles (matching the row's 7-7.5 mi figures), while the park route brief gives 8-9 miles and other listings put Paradise-Muir at ~4.4 mi and Muir-summit at ~4-4.75 mi (8.4-9 mi one way, ~18 mi round trip, matching the itinerary). What would settle it: a measured one-way track length Paradise to Columbia Crest via the Cleaver.

results.fact: Camp Muir reservable vs walk-up split
results.evidence: Re-read today, the two official park pages still disagree: the wilderness permit page says approximately two-thirds of summer permits are reservable, while the climbing page says roughly 50% of each camp is held for walk-up registration. The two non-bivy fields follow the climbing page; the only two-thirds copy is bivy[0], which this pass may not patch. What would settle it: the park reconciling the two pages (or a current Recreation.gov inventory count for Camp Muir).

The route description gives only the route length (8,000 ft, Grade IV) and a 10,000 ft bivy reached up the North Mowich Glacier; no source states a car-to-car gain for this route, and gain_ft may not be computed from elevations. What would settle it: a source stating the round-trip gain from Mowich Lake.
